standard.title: Elements of drama in play
standard.description: use the elements of drama and imagination in dramatic play and/or process drama
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use play and imagination to discover possibilities and develop ideas (Foundation). They can engage in purposeful exploration of materials, voice and movement.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use the elements of drama — role, place, situation, language and movement — and imagination in dramatic play and/or process drama.

nodes.label: Understanding the elements of drama
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can name and recognise the basic elements of drama — role, place, situation, language, movement — in drama they experience and create.
nodes.minimum_width: Student can use at least two drama element terms appropriately when describing their own or others' drama.
nodes.typical_width: Students understand and use appropriate drama terminology (role, place, situation, language, movement, dramatic play, process drama, pretending, audience, theatre, performance, actors) when discussing drama they have made and/or experienced.
wider: Students explore how elements combine differently in different forms — comparing dramatic play to a class performance — and name what changes
Students use props from familiar contexts (empty containers, clothing, toys) to explore how physical objects create or signal role and place
nodes.hinge_reason: If students lack element vocabulary and conceptual awareness, they cannot intentionally use elements in their drama-making — subsequent nodes about taking roles and developing situations lack a shared language.

response_modes.reason: Explicitly introduce each element with concrete examples from drama students have just experienced; use questioning ('What role were you playing? What was the place?') to make the elements visible.

success_criteria: Student correctly uses at least two drama element terms when discussing drama
Student can identify an element of drama (e.g. role, place) in a drama they have participated in or observed

nodes.label: Taking on role in dramatic play
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can take on a role purposefully in dramatic play or process drama, developing ideas through that role.
nodes.minimum_width: Student takes on a specific role in dramatic play and makes decisions from within that role.
nodes.typical_width: Students take on roles in dramatic play focusing on creating situations; they stay in role when participating in improvised drama; they develop ideas from texts (children's literature, images) into character and situation.
wider: Students explore a range of role types — from characters in familiar stories to imagined roles in invented scenarios — and consider how different roles produce different perspectives
Students participate in process drama with teacher-in-role, accepting and responding to the teacher's character within the fictional world

response_modes.reason: Staying in role requires repeated practice; students need multiple short experiences of role-taking before they can sustain it through a more complex dramatic sequence.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The variety of role types and dramatic contexts available — puppets, teacher-in-role, Readers' Theatre, movement drama — offers rich opportunity for advancing students to deepen their understanding of how role shapes perspective and action.
success_criteria: Student takes on a named or implied role and sustains it for the duration of a short dramatic play sequence
Student makes at least one decision or contribution from within the role
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The variety of role types and dramatic contexts available — puppets, teacher-in-role, Readers' Theatre, movement drama — offers rich opportunity for advancing students to deepen their understanding of how role shapes perspective and action.

nodes.label: Using elements to develop dramatic situations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use elements of drama — particularly role, place, situation and movement — intentionally to develop and sustain a dramatic situation.
nodes.minimum_width: Student uses at least two elements intentionally within a sustained dramatic play or process drama sequence.
nodes.typical_width: Students use language, movement and role to develop situations in dramatic play; they use facial expressions and body to show role and situation; they brainstorm and discuss situations and improvise drama that develops those ideas.
wider: Students explore how manipulating one element (e.g. changing the place, adding a new character) transforms the dramatic situation and what it communicates
Students use movement-based drama or mime to show role and situation without words, exploring how movement communicates meaning independently of language

response_modes.reason: This node is where element knowledge and role-taking come together into purposeful drama-making. Support students to make intentional choices about which elements to use and how.

success_criteria: Student uses at least two elements of drama intentionally in a dramatic play or process drama sequence
Student can describe which elements they were using and what they were trying to show
